name: Hananiah (Son of Zerubbabel, descendant of David)
title: Descendant of David in the royal lineage
summary: Hananiah was a son of Zerubbabel, who served as governor of Judah after returning from the Babylonian exile. As a descendant of King David, he belonged to the royal line preserved through the exile and the period of return. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Chronicles as part of David's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in David's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hananiah is listed as one of the sons of Zerubbabel in the Davidic line continued after the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Part of the royal lineage
keyEvents.description: As a descendant of David through Zerubbabel, Hananiah represents the continuity of the royal line of Judah after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Zerubbabel's sons listed
keyEvents.description: The book of Chronicles gives a detailed overview of Zerubbabel's children, where Hananiah is mentioned along with his brothers and a sister as important descendants of David's house.

keyEvents.title: Hananiah's descendants
keyEvents.description: Hananiah's sons Pelatiah and Isaiah are mentioned as part of the continued Davidic line in the post-exilic period.
